transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve just been feeling really low most days. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s like I’m sitting at the bottom of a dark hole, and even when I’m around people I know, I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. I wasn’t sure if that was enough of a reason to come in, but… it’s been hard.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um… it’s been a while, I guess. Probably about a year and two months now. It started after that fall I had on an HVAC job last fall, when I hurt my back, and then… everything just kind of started unraveling from there. I hope that makes sense.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

Not really… I mean, I try not to be negative about it, but things I used to love just don’t feel the same. I used to hike, paint, go tinker around at the makerspace… even figuring out a tricky install at work used to feel kind of satisfying. Now I’ll just stare at the supplies or let people’s calls go unanswered because it feels like… I don’t know, like none of it is worth even starting. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often feel anxious or worried?

I’m… not sure, honestly. I mean, I worry about things like anyone does, I guess, but I don’t know if I’d call it anxious exactly. Maybe I’m not explaining that right. What do you mean by “often,” like… most days?
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasurable?

I wish I could say yes… and maybe there are tiny moments here and there, but not really like before. I used to really love hiking, painting, messing around at the makerspace, even figuring out a tough install at work. Now I’ll sit there with the supplies in front of me and just… not start. Or I ignore calls from people who’d normally get me to do something. It’s like none of it feels worth the effort. Is that… is that what you’re asking?
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but the things I used to really look forward to—hiking, painting, tinkering at the makerspace, even solving a tricky install at work—they just don’t pull me in anymore. I’ll have the supplies right there and just stare at them, or I’ll ignore calls from people because starting anything feels… not worth it. Does that make sense?
Have you ever thought about harming yourself or wished you were dead?

I… I don’t want to worry you or make it sound worse than it is. But yes, I’ve had thoughts like… maybe everyone would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. And sometimes when the pain and the money stuff all piles up, I catch myself thinking about ending it. It scares me, though. I’m sorry, is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Um… I don’t know if it’s significant, exactly. I haven’t been keeping track like I should. My eating’s been kind of all over the place. Some days I’ll mostly just have coffee because food sounds awful, and then late at night I’ll pick at whatever’s in the cabinet… not really because I want it, more just… because it’s there. Is that helpful?
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still?

Yeah… I think more the slow part than restless. I mean, I can still do things, so I don’t want to overstate it, but everything feels like it takes so much longer now. Getting from the couch to the kitchen, answering a simple question… it’s like I’m moving through water or something. People have asked if I’m okay because I’m moving so slowly. Is that what you mean?
Do you ever feel like you're so restless that you can't sit still?

Not really the restless kind, no… I mean, I don’t think I’m pacing or unable to sit still. It’s more the opposite. Everything I do is slow now, like just getting from the couch to the kitchen or answering something simple takes longer than it should. People keep asking if I’m okay because I move like I’m underwater. Does that answer it?
Do you ever feel like you're so restless that you can't sit still?

Not so much that I can’t sit still, no. If anything, it’s… the other way. I’m slower than I used to be. Like even getting from the couch to the kitchen, or answering a simple question, it takes me longer than it should. People have asked if I’m okay because I guess I’m moving like I’m underwater. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Do you find that your low mood or energy levels change with the seasons?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed a seasonal pattern, honestly. I mean, I don’t think it’s clearly worse in winter or better in summer or anything like that. It feels more… just kind of there. Is that what you’re asking?
Do you find that your mood or energy levels change throughout the day?

I’m not totally sure. I haven’t really tracked it hour by hour or anything. It doesn’t jump out to me like, “oh, mornings are always worse” or “I perk up at night.” It just feels kind of… steady, I guess. If that makes sense?
Have you ever felt this low or experienced a period like this before in your life?

I… I don’t really know. I mean, I’ve had rough times before, like anybody, but I’m not sure I’d say it was like this. Nothing that I can clearly point to and say, yes, that was the same. Is that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you usually feel your lowest at a specific time of day?

I don’t think so… not that I’ve really noticed. It’s more like I feel low most of the time, but I couldn’t honestly tell you there’s a certain hour where it’s always the worst. Is that okay to say if I’m not sure?
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt as low as you do now for at least two weeks?

I’m not sure… I don’t want to say no if I’m forgetting something, but I also can’t think of a time that was clearly this low for that long. I’ve had bad stretches, definitely, but nothing I can confidently compare to now. Does that answer it okay?
Do you usually feel your lowest at a specific time of day?

I’m sorry, I don’t think I’ve noticed a certain time exactly. It’s more… most days it’s just there, like this heavy dark feeling I can’t get out from under. Even if I’m around people I know, I still feel kind of stuck at the bottom, if that makes sense. I don’t want to overstate it, but it feels pretty hopeless a lot of the time.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt as low as you do now for at least two weeks?

I… I’m not totally sure how to compare it to before. I’ve had times where I felt pretty down, but this time is what made me come in, because most days it feels like I’m just sitting at the bottom of this dark hole. Even when I’m around people I know, I can’t really shake that heavy, hopeless feeling.

Sorry, is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had more than one period in your life where you felt as low as you do now?

I don’t think I can say for sure there’s been more than one, honestly. I’ve had low times, but this current one is the one that really made me come in. Most days it feels like I’m down at the bottom of a dark hole, and even being around people I know doesn’t really lift that heavy, hopeless feeling.

I hope that answers what you’re asking.
Have you experienced a period of significant depression like this one before in your life?

I’m not sure I’d call it the same as this before. I’ve had rough stretches, sure, but I don’t know if they were really… significant in the way this feels now. This is the one that feels hard enough that I felt like I should talk to someone.

Does that answer it okay?
